scope: Every tracked outer-repository documentation file: all tracked *.md outside the upstream/llama.cpp submodule, plus the two tracked reference JSON documents under docs/reference/. Submodule internals are out of scope; upstream source is cited as evidence but not audited.

dispositions.updated: A disagreement with the implementation was found and the document was corrected in this pass.
dispositions.aligned: Checked against the named implementation evidence in this pass and found consistent. Not a claim that every line was independently re-derived.
dispositions.historical: A dated record of a past observation. Preserved unchanged, and deliberately NOT re-verified against current implementation, because it does not describe current state.
dispositions.added: Added after the original audit; inventoried and checked against the cited source during its own continuation.

limits: This is a documentation-consistency audit. It makes no quality, performance or model-capability claim.
No model was loaded, no GPU was touched, no service was started or stopped, and no throughput was measured while producing it.
It reports no current runtime health. The qualification state, router residency and host conflicts observed during the pass are runtime facts that change, and none are recorded here.
'aligned' means no disagreement was found by the checks named in each entry, not that the document is proven correct.
mechanical_checks: Every relative markdown link and heading anchor across all tracked documentation resolves.

Every repository path named in a fenced command block exists on disk, excluding two documented placeholders (an experimental worktree the runbook tells the operator to create, and an ignored evidence filename template).
Every *.service name resolves to a tracked unit under services/systemd/, excluding the phaseN template placeholder.
Every HERMES_* variable named in documentation appears in tracked code.
Every 127.0.0.1:<port> in documentation matches a port in a tracked unit, env file or script.
The CONFIGURATION.md alias table is compared field by field against llama-models.ini by an added test.

entries.finding: Sidecars 'run at Nice=5 and best-effort I/O priority so they never win a resource fight against the interactive router'.

entries.change: Kept the unit's intent and qualified the mechanism: Nice weights CPU scheduling only and does not arbitrate VRAM residency or GPU submission, the qualification runs at the same Nice, the ionice setting is one notch below default and inert under a scheduler that ignores priorities. Names --models-max 1, the quiet-host wait and inference-conflict classification as the actual serialization.
